findings.title: `fire_unit_until` cannot stop the unit early: `subprocess.run` blocks on `mt-run`, which only exits when the unit ends
findings.description: Description: `fire_unit_until` calls `run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], sudo=True, check=False, stream=True)`, and `run()` is `subprocess.run(...)` — it blocks until the child exits. The installed wrapper (`deploy/mt-run`, `start_and_stream`, installed to `/usr/local/bin/mt-run` by `install-production.sh:183`) does `systemctl start --no-block` and then `while is_running "${unit}"; do sleep 2; done` — it exits only when the unit is inactive. So in production the cutover thread sits inside `subprocess.run` for the *entire* pass (trailing + unbounded backfill), exactly the ten-hour wait this diff exists to remove; `wait_for_unit_or_line` is only reached after the unit has already ended, where `reached and unit_active(unit)` is always False and no stop is ever issued. `fire_unit_until` degenerates to `fire_unit`. The unit test that claims to cover this (`TestBoundedFiringAndRecord.test_the_minute_firing_stops_once_the_trailing_phase_completes` in `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py`) patches `cutover_common.run` to return instantly, so it exercises the poll/stop logic against a control flow that never occurs in production — the external boundary's real behavior (mt-run blocks until the unit ends) is not modeled, which is the false-confidence trap AGENTS.md warns about. Related: the printed claim "Ctrl-C only detaches, the script keeps waiting" is also false in practice — the cutover, `sudo`, and `mt-run` share one process group, so Ctrl-C raises `KeyboardInterrupt` in the cutover (the `finally` releases timers, but the script dies rather than "keeps waiting"); the unit keeps running unattended. A viable fix: start the unit with a non-blocking command the operator is already granted (`sudo systemctl start mt-*` is in `MT_UNITS`) and poll the journal from the script, or give `mt-run` a detach-and-return mode; either way the waiting must happen in the cutover process, not inside a blocking `subprocess.run`.

findings.title: New sudoers grant `mt-run *` is far wider than the cutover scripts issue, contradicting the file's own "nothing wider" header
findings.description: Description: The file header promises "Exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider". The scripts issue `mt-run minute`, `mt-run daily`, `mt-run kalshi`, and `mt-run data kalshi status --json` — but `Cmnd_Alias MT_RUN = /usr/local/bin/mt-run *` grants the operator *every* `mt` CLI subcommand with the production environment: the wrapper's pass-through branch (`run_production_mt` in `deploy/mt-run`) execs the production `mt` binary with `/etc/manta-trading.env` sourced, including destructive maintenance that takes its DB URLs from that ambient file (`data caggs repair` → drop_chunks/refresh, `data rechunk`, `data migrate apply`, …). That is precisely the "maintenance tooling with ambient-URL targeting" posture the production-protection rules in sql.md push back against, and it is not exercised by any script this diff names. `MT_READ` has the same shape at lower severity: `cat /etc/manta-trading.env` hands the operator every production secret (EODHD keys, application and maintenance DB URLs), while the actual need (in shared `cutover_common.verify_migrate_target`) is only a host/port/dbname comparison. Recommend enumerating the specific `mt-run` invocations and replacing the env-file read with a root-side helper that returns only URL identities. (Minor: `MT_UNITS`'s `mt-*` globs are broader than the four named units, and `install()` in `cutover_common.py` resolves its own path while `MT_INSTALL` hardcodes `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data` — a relocated checkout fails with permission denied, which is acceptable only if the mismatch is documented in the sudoers header.)

findings.title: Bar-timestamp parsing is duplicated between `bar_timestamp` and `_bar_to_row` and can diverge
findings.description: Description: `bar_timestamp` "mirrors `_bar_to_row`" (minute.py) for the epoch/ISO timestamp, but `_bar_to_row` additionally skips bars with missing/malformed prices (documented to actually occur: EODHD null prices, 2026-08-14). A response that contains exactly one bar inside a judged session, where that bar has a valid timestamp but an unusable price, will be counted as session-coverage by `judge_chunk_by_sessions` while `_insert_minute_bars` skips the row — the chunk is judged SUCCESS, `_advance_minute_gap` deletes the gap row, and the session is stored empty: the same silent-truncation failure #22 removes, reintroduced in rarer form. AGENTS.md forbids duplicated logic; the old third copy (`_latest_bar_dt`) was deleted in this diff, which is good, but the remaining pair should share one parser — ideally the chunk is judged on the rows that were actually inserted, not the raw provider bars.

findings.title: `CaggFreshness.stale` omits the cagg policy's 4-hour end_offset
findings.description: Description: The probe reports fresh when `last_successful_finish >= newest_bar_written`, but `minute_4hour_ohlcv`'s refresh policy (migration 035/053) materializes only buckets fully inside `[R - 3d, R - 4h]`, so a refresh that finished shortly after a bar was written has not necessarily materialized that bar's bucket. The sibling `cagg_freshness._resolve_threshold` treats `end_offset` as load-bearing for exactly this reason. For the judged sessions in practice (NYSE closes at 17:00/20:00 UTC, judged at the next firing + 3h) the last bucket is always closed long before judging, so this is not a live misjudgment today — but the property "fresh ⇒ every session bar is materialized" does not hold by construction, and a calendar with a close within ~4h of a firing would break it. Worth a comment or a `+ end_offset` margin so the assumption is explicit.

findings.title: `--verify`'s WAIT state exits with code 2 (EXIT_REFUSED), conflating "not judgeable yet" with "refused/failed"
findings.description: Description: `run_verify` now returns `False` on `[WAIT]`, and `main` maps any False to `EXIT_REFUSED` (2). The cutover script copes by scanning the text, but a human or CI consumer of `repair_921_minute_sessions.py --verify` gets exit 2 indistinguishable from a genuine refusal or failure. WAIT is an "again in an hour" state, not a verdict; a distinct exit code (or at least documented code) would keep the three states separable.

findings.title: `mt-minute-pass.timer` still claims the minute pass is "staggered 30 minutes behind" the daily pass
findings.description: Description: Both OnCalendar times moved to 04:05/13:05, and the 04:05 placement's real reason is documented on the constant (`MINUTE_PASS_FIRING_TIMES_UTC`: the first firing must sit *after* EODHD publishes the day, ~03:00+ UTC). The unit's `[Unit] Description` and the `[Timer]` comment still assert "staggered 30 minutes behind mt-daily-pass.timer" — true only for 13:05 vs 12:35 (04:05 is 3h30m after 00:35). An operator reading the timer file gets the wrong mental model of why 04:05 was chosen; the same diff already updated the cross-reference in `mt-kalshi-pass.timer`.

findings.title: Two of the diff's import blocks are now unsorted under the repo's ruff-I (ASCII) convention
findings.description: Description: Pre-existing blocks in these files follow case-sensitive ASCII order (`CutoverError, fire_unit, …`; `CheckReport, RepairScanTimeout, build_truncated_day_index, …`). The diff inserts `NOTES_DIR, fire_unit_until, start_log` *before* `CutoverError` in `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py` and `cagg_freshness_for_session` *before* `CheckReport` in `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py` — `ruff check --select I` would reorder both. CI runs no lint job (the workflow is tag-only publishing), so nothing enforces it; fix at the next touch to keep the mechanical rule real.

findings.title: Standing per-cycle daemon logic now lives in a one-time slice-named repair module
findings.description: Description: `minute.py` now calls `build_truncated_day_index` (and the cutover/verify paths call `cagg_freshness_for_session`) on **every** minute cycle, but both live in `repair_921.py`, whose docstring frames it as the one-time 2026-07-16 truncation repair. When that repair script is retired, the daemon still imports "repair_921" for permanent functionality, and the module will hold logic that is not repair-specific. Consider moving the truncated-day index and the cagg-freshness probe into `minute_coverage`/`compute_missing_ranges` (or a standing `truncation` module) while the slice is still fresh.

findings.title: `start_log` runs before `preflight` validates the working directory, and same-minute reruns clobber the record
findings.description: Description: `main` opens `NOTES_DIR / "921-cutover-…Z.log"` (relative: `project-documents/user/notes`) before `preflight` refuses non-checkout-root execution — a wrong-CWD run creates a stray directory tree and log somewhere else, then dies. Also the filename is minute-granularity and `start_log` uses `write_text` (truncate): two runs started in the same minute would overwrite the first run's narration — the record this feature was added to preserve. Opening the log after the CWD check, and refusing/numbering on an existing path, would close both.

findings.title: Load-test tier for the new per-cycle DB work is unverified
findings.description: Description: The python rules require at least one load test for code on the network/concurrency paths, and this diff adds per-cycle work to the minute pass: a universe-wide truncation scan under a 600s `statement_timeout` on a pooled connection (once per cycle, ~8s measured — fine in isolation) plus one `fetch_session_bounds` round trip per chunk (~13k+ extra indexed queries per pass). I could not confirm a `tests/load/` entry exercising `run_minute_cycle` with these additions at production scale; please verify one exists or add one, since unit tests here cannot show pool pressure (max_size=4) or the scan's interaction with the 300s session timeout it temporarily overrides.

findings.title: Timer/constant drift guard and session-judgement logic verified consistent
findings.description: Description: Verified against the underlying files: `MINUTE_PASS_FIRING_TIMES_UTC = (time(4,5), time(13,5))` matches both `OnCalendar` lines in `deploy/systemd/mt-minute-pass.timer`, and `TestMinutePassTimerMatchesTheConstant` asserts set equality in both directions, so a future schedule move fails CI. `collecting_firing_finished_at`'s 07:05 boundary math checks out for both the 20:00 and 17:00 closes, and the updated `test_data_health.py` cases pin it. `sessions_without_bars`' `(open, close]` predicate matches `find_truncated_days`' `newest <= open` signature (agreement asserted by existing tests), the spillover case from the incident is covered end-to-end in `TestChunkJudgedBySessions`, and the truncated-day index is correctly scoped to the trailing phase only (`test_only_the_trailing_phase_receives_the_index`). The UTC reformatting in `check_minute_session_mass` is correct for any connection timezone since psycopg returns tz-aware values.
